MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #1
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which Roman numeral stands for 4? (1 mark)
   A. IIII
   B. IV
   C. VIIII
   D. VX

2. Which Roman numeral stands for 3? (1 mark)
   A. III
   B. VX
   C. IIII
   D. VIIII

3. Which of these is a multiple of 12? (1 mark)
   A. 85
   B. 84
   C. 83
   D. 86

4. What is the total value of the digit 4 in 9,481? (1 mark)
   A. 4,000
   B. 40
   C. 4
   D. 400

5. What is the rule of the pattern 125, 250, 375, 500? (1 mark)
   A. add 250
   B. add 125
   C. add 175
   D. subtract 125

6. Which number must be added to 3,425 to make 5,743? (1 mark)
   A. 2,318
   B. 9,168
   C. 2,418
   D. 2,308

7. Work out 19 × 31. (1 mark)
   A. 76
   B. 579
   C. 589
   D. 599

8. A packet holds 40 sweets. How many sweets are in 15 packets? (1 mark)
   A. 580 sweets
   B. 700 sweets
   C. 600 sweets
   D. 590 sweets

9. Work out 32 × 21. (1 mark)
   A. 662
   B. 96
   C. 672
   D. 682

10. In 56 ÷ 8 = 7, the number 8 is called the (1 mark)
   A. remainder
   B. dividend
   C. divisor
   D. quotient

11. A rectangle is cut into 8 equal parts and 3 of the parts are shaded. What fraction of the rectangle is shaded? (1 mark)
   A. 8/3
   B. 3/8
   C. 5/8
   D. 3/5

12. Beth writes some more fractions. Which of these is an improper fraction? (1 mark)
   A. 3 1/2
   B. 2/9
   C. 11/5
   D. 1/2

13. A circle is cut into 8 equal parts and 3 parts are shaded. What fraction is not shaded? (1 mark)
   A. 8/5
   B. 5/3
   C. 3/8
   D. 5/8

14. Change 3 2/5 to an improper fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 5/5
   B. 17/5
   C. 18/5
   D. 15/5

15. A hundred square has 7 of its small squares shaded. Which decimal shows the shaded part? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 0.07
   C. 0.007
   D. 0.7

16. Write 0.8 as a fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 8/100
   B. 8/10
   C. 80/10
   D. 1/8

17. A hundred square has 35 of its small squares shaded. Which decimal shows the shaded part? (1 mark)
   A. 0.35
   B. 35
   C. 0.035
   D. 3.5

18. Which is greater, 0.5 or 0.45? (1 mark)
   A. 0.5
   B. They are equal
   C. It cannot be told
   D. 0.45

19. What is half a metre in centimetres? (1 mark)
   A. 500 cm
   B. 20 cm
   C. 50 cm
   D. 5 cm

20. Change 640 cm to metres and centimetres. (1 mark)
   A. 64 cm
   B. 6 m 90 cm
   C. 6 m 40 cm
   D. 7 m 40 cm

21. A pencil starts at the 4 cm mark on a ruler and ends at the 12 cm mark. How long is the pencil? (1 mark)
   A. 8 cm
   B. 9 cm
   C. 12 cm
   D. 16 cm

22. What is 1 m 35 cm + 2 m 85 cm? (1 mark)
   A. 4 m 10 cm
   B. 5 m 20 cm
   C. 3 m 20 cm
   D. 4 m 20 cm

23. Rectangle P has 4 rows and 9 columns. Rectangle Q has 5 rows and 8 columns. Which has the bigger area? (1 mark)
   A. They are equal
   B. Rectangle Q
   C. Rectangle P
   D. It cannot be told

24. Which sum finds the area of a rectangle with 4 rows and 6 columns? (1 mark)
   A. 4 × 6
   B. 6 ÷ 4
   C. 4 − 6
   D. 4 + 6

25. A rectangle has an area of 72 square units and 9 rows. How many columns does it have? (1 mark)
   A. 63
   B. 9
   C. 8
   D. 81

26. A beam balance is level with rice in one pan and a 1/2 kg mass and a 1/4 kg mass in the other pan. What is the mass of the rice? (1 mark)
   A. 3/4 kg
   B. 1/4 kg
   C. 1/2 kg
   D. 1 kg

27. Change 17 days to weeks and days. (1 mark)
   A. 2 weeks 3 days
   B. 3 weeks 2 days
   C. 3 weeks
   D. 2 weeks 4 days

28. Wekesa wakes up at half past six in the morning. How do we write this time? (1 mark)
   A. 6:30 p.m.
   B. 6:03 a.m.
   C. 6:30 noon
   D. 6:30 a.m.

29. Change 48 hours to days. (1 mark)
   A. 0.8 days
   B. 4 days
   C. 2 days
   D. 3 days

30. What is 2 h 45 min + 1 h 30 min? (1 mark)
   A. 4 h 25 min
   B. 3 h 15 min
   C. 4 h 15 min
   D. 4 h 5 min

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Work out 36 × 24 by first multiplying by the ones and then by the tens. (3 marks)

32. A signboard has four straight sides. Two sides are 50 cm and two are 30 cm. All four corners are square. Name the shape and give a reason. (3 marks)

33. State whether 1,468 and 3,975 are even or odd. Give a reason for each. (3 marks)

34. Work out 6,003 − 2,475 and check your answer by adding. (4 marks)

35. Subtract 2 hours 35 minutes from 5 hours 20 minutes. (3 marks)

36. Ten vehicles passed: 5 matatus, 2 boda bodas, 2 buses and 1 lorry. Draw a table to show this data. (3 marks)

37. A bag has a mass of 5 kg. Musa takes out 1 1/2 kg of beans. What mass is left in the bag? (2 marks)

38. Give two differences between perimeter and area. (3 marks)

39. Express 23/6 as a mixed fraction. (3 marks)

40. Arrange 605, 560, 650 and 506 from smallest to largest. (3 marks)

41. Mama Kioko sells 3 bags of mangoes (m) and 2 bags of oranges (o) on Monday, then 1 bag of mangoes and 4 bags of oranges on Tuesday. Write an expression and simplify it. (4 marks)

42. Divide 58 by 4 and give the remainder. (3 marks)

43. A trader has 25 kg of rice. She sells 7 1/2 kg to one customer and 6 3/4 kg to another. How much rice does she have left? (5 marks)

44. Add 6,478 and 2,355 and check by estimating to the nearest ten. (4 marks)

45. Wangari buys 24 exercise books at Ksh 18 each. Estimate the total cost by rounding to the nearest ten, then work out the exact cost. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #1 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — IV
   4 is written IV. I before V is 5 − 1.

2. A — III
   3 is written III. Letters after a bigger letter are added.

3. B — 84
   84 = 12 × 7, so 84 is a multiple of 12.

4. D — 400
   The digit 4 is in the hundreds place, so its total value is 4 × 100 = 400.

5. B — add 125
   Each number is 125 more than the one before it, so the rule is add 125.

6. A — 2,318
   5,743 − 3,425 = 2,318. Check: 3,425 + 2,318 = 5,743.

7. C — 589
   19 × 1 = 19 and 19 × 30 = 570. 19 + 570 = 589.

8. C — 600 sweets
   Multiply to find the total. The answer is 600 sweets.

9. C — 672
   32 × 1 = 32 and 32 × 20 = 640. 32 + 640 = 672.

10. C — divisor
   The number we divide by is the divisor. 56 is the dividend and 7 is the quotient.

11. B — 3/8
   The whole has 8 equal parts and 3 are shaded, so 3/8 is shaded.

12. C — 11/5
   In an improper fraction the numerator is equal to or bigger than the denominator. 11/5 is one whole or more.

13. D — 5/8
   Not shaded: 8 − 3 = 5 parts, so 5/8.

14. B — 17/5
   3 × 5 = 15 and 15 + 2 = 17. The denominator stays 5, so the answer is 17/5.

15. B — 0.07
   7 out of 100 squares is 7/100 = 0.07.

16. B — 8/10
   The last digit of 0.8 is in the tenths place, so the denominator is 10. 0.8 = 8/10.

17. A — 0.35
   35 out of 100 squares is 35/100 = 0.35.

18. A — 0.5
   Compare the tenths first. 0.5 is greater than 0.45.

19. C — 50 cm
   1 m = 100 cm. Use this to change between the two units: half a metre in centimetres is 50 cm.

20. C — 6 m 40 cm
   640 ÷ 100 = 6 remainder 40. So 640 cm = 6 m 40 cm.

21. A — 8 cm
   Subtract the start from the end: 12 − 4 = 8 cm.

22. D — 4 m 20 cm
   Change to centimetres: 135 + 285 = 420 cm = 4 m 20 cm.

23. B — Rectangle Q
   P = 4 × 9 = 36 and Q = 5 × 8 = 40. Rectangle Q has the bigger area.

24. A — 4 × 6
   Area is the number of rows multiplied by the number of columns.

25. C — 8
   Rows × columns = 72, so columns = 72 ÷ 9 = 8.

26. A — 3/4 kg
   1/2 + 1/4 = 2/4 + 1/4 = 3/4 kg.

27. A — 2 weeks 3 days
   17 ÷ 7 = 2 remainder 3, so 17 days = 2 weeks 3 days.

28. D — 6:30 a.m.
   Times from midnight to noon use a.m. and times from noon to midnight use p.m. The correct answer is 6:30 a.m..

29. C — 2 days
   48 ÷ 24 = 2 days.

30. C — 4 h 15 min
   Add the minutes and hours, then change 60 minutes into 1 hour. The answer is 4 h 15 min.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: 864
   Working / marking points: 36 × 4 = 144 (1 mark); 36 × 20 = 720 (1 mark); 144 + 720 = 864 (1 mark).

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: A rectangle, because opposite sides are equal but not all sides are equal.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the name, 1 mark for opposite sides equal, 1 mark for not all sides equal.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: 1,468 is even because it ends in 8. 3,975 is odd because it ends in 5.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct classification with a reason (2 marks) and 1 mark for referring to the ones digit.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: 3,528. Check: 3,528 + 2,475 = 6,003.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for correct regrouping across the zeros, 1 mark for the answer, 1 mark for the check.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2 hours 45 minutes
   Working / marking points: Change 5 h 20 min to 4 h 80 min (1 mark); 80 − 35 = 45 min (1 mark); 4 − 2 = 2 h, so 2 h 45 min (1 mark).

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: A table with a title and two columns, Vehicle and Number, with rows matatu 5, boda boda 2, bus 2, lorry 1 and total 10.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for title and headings, 1 mark for all four rows correct, 1 mark for the total 10.

37. (2 marks)
   Answer: 3 1/2 kg
   Working / marking points: 5 − 1 1/2 = 3 1/2. 1 mark for the subtraction and 1 mark for the unit.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: Perimeter is the distance round the edge and is measured in units of length such as cm. Area is the flat surface inside the shape and is measured in square units.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning of each and 1 mark for the units.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3 5/6
   Working / marking points: 23 ÷ 6 = 3 remainder 5 (2 marks). Write 3 5/6 with the same denominator (1 mark).

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: 506, 560, 605, 650
   Working / marking points: Compare hundreds first, then tens. 1 mark for each correct pair of positions, up to 3 marks.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: 3m + 2o + m + 4o = 4m + 6o
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the expression, 1 mark for 4m, 1 mark for 6o, 1 mark for the final answer.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: 14 remainder 2
   Working / marking points: 5 tens ÷ 4 = 1 remainder 1 (1 mark); 18 ÷ 4 = 4 remainder 2 (1 mark); answer 14 R 2 (1 mark).

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: 10 3/4 kg
   Working / marking points: Total sold: 7 1/2 + 6 3/4 = 7 2/4 + 6 3/4 = 13 5/4 = 14 1/4 kg (3 marks). 25 − 14 1/4 = 10 3/4 kg (2 marks).

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Exact 8,833. Estimate 6,480 + 2,360 = 8,840, which is close.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the exact sum with regrouping, 1 mark for rounding both numbers, 1 mark for the estimate.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: Estimate: 20 × 20 = 400. Exact: 24 × 18 = 432 shillings.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for rounding both numbers, 1 mark for 400, 1 mark for the exact working (24 × 8 = 192 and 24 × 10 = 240), 1 mark for 432.
